# origincloud_network_resolver_policy (Resource)

How a VPC's resolver answers names outside the platform's own.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project` (String) The project the resolver policy is in. Changing it replaces the resolver policy.
- `region` (String) The region the resolver policy is in. Changing it replaces the resolver policy.

### Optional

- `relay_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the resolver relays names it can't answer itself to `upstream_servers`. Off, it answers only the platform's own names.
- `tags` (Map of String) Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows.
- `upstream_servers` (List of String) The resolvers to relay to, at most 5 IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, tried in order. At least one while `relay_enabled` is on.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the resolver policy was created. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.
- `creator` (String) The principal that created the resolver policy, by its full name on iam: `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/users/{user}`, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or a platform service agent's or service's name when the platform did.
- `id` (String) The resolver policy's full resource name, `//network.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/regions/{region}/resolverPolicies/{resolver_policy}`: what an argument that refers to the resolver policy takes. `name` is the relative name, without the host.
- `name` (String) The policy's resource name.
- `project_default` (Boolean) Whether this is the project's default policy in its region, which a VPC without a resolver policy association relays through. Change it with `SetDefaultResolverPolicy`.
